clue.text: Help to grab American's purse

blocks.note: to lend a hand is to help
to bag something is to grab it

explanation.surface: A thief assisting in snatching a visitor's purse.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English a purse is what Britons call a handbag, so the definition needs the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans use purse for the bag a woman carries her belongings in, which British speakers call by another name.

clue.text: Prisoner has got crack and Ecstasy

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An inmate found in possession of crack cocaine and ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack and Ecstasy both read as drugs, but only Ecstasy is; crack is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person seized and held captive, often to force others to meet demands.

clue.text: Tending to run about on grass

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the preceding word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to grass is to inform on someone, as is to sing

explanation.surface: A groundsman's habit of jogging around on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass and sing are both slang for informing to the police. 'Tending to' looks like 'inclined to', but here it means caring for.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing a patient means looking after them, so nursing and tending to are interchangeable.

clue.text: Bishop's final tirade

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; the 's means 'is' or 'has', joining it on
the last is the final one

explanation.surface: A bishop's last angry sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a furious verbal attack, the same as a long angry speech of criticism.

clue.text: Dog fouled tea garden

indicators.note: something fouled is messed up, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog has made a mess in the café garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant breed of hound originally used in Germany for hunting boar.

clue.text: Dad tried dancing and had fun

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and swap places, so the word beside it is rearranged

blocks.note: Pa is an informal word for father
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A father attempted some dancing and enjoyed himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad is not part of the anagram: he stays as PA while only 'tried' dances, giving PARTIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To party is to celebrate at a lively social gathering, so someone who did so enjoyed themselves.

clue.text: Essentially, peers must be reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political demand that the House of Lords be overhauled.
explanation.walkthrough: Peers sit in the House of Lords, whose reform is a long-running British debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Per se is Latin for 'by itself', used to mean intrinsically, in its own nature.

clue.text: People nag Sir Ivor, perhaps

blocks.note: a race is a people sharing descent
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: Folk pester a knight called Sir Ivor.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Ivor sounds like a knight, but he was a champion thoroughbred who won the 1968 Derby; 'nag' is a horse, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Ivor was a famous Derby-winning thoroughbred, and 'perhaps' marks him as one instance of the category.

clue.text: First in Information Technology, second in history, Latin and algebra

indicators.note: second means the letter in position two of each of the following words is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the standard abbreviation for computing
second letter of history
second letter of Latin
second letter of algebra

explanation.surface: A school report: top marks in computing, runner-up in three other subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First in' looks like a letter-picking instruction, but First is the definition and 'in' is a piece; 'second' applies to all three subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means occurring at the beginning, as in the initial stage, the same as first.

clue.text: Extremely dingy and unpleasant house

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of dingy
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: An estate agent's frank verdict on a grim, dirty property.
explanation.walkthrough: House here is a ruling family, as in the House of Windsor, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers from one family, which is also called a royal house.

clue.text: Annoy Mrs Una E. Smith, say

indicators.note: to annoy is to disturb, and disturbed letters are knocked out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to irritate a woman called Mrs Una E. Smith.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd initial E is the giveaway that 'Mrs Una E' is fodder rather than a name; Smith is then the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Smith is a very common family name, and 'say' marks it as one instance of a family name.

clue.text: Once police in Belfast start to tell one about disturbance

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the Royal Ulster Constabulary policed Northern Ireland until 2001
opening letter of tell
the Roman numeral for one
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Former Belfast police begin telling someone about a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' signals a body that no longer exists: the RUC was replaced by the Police Service of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy quarrel or uproar, which is a kind of commotion or upset.

clue.text: Patrician, ultimately pessimist, and liberal European philosopher

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: aristo is short for aristocrat, a noble
last letter of pessimist
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A list describing an aristocratic, gloomy but broad-minded European thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as adjectives all describing the philosopher, but each word supplies a piece of ARISTOTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato, whose work founded much of Western logic and science.

clue.text: They will inherit from their sister

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the words that follow, spanning a word break

blocks.note: found running across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Siblings expecting to come into money from their sister's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs are the people entitled to receive property or titles when someone dies.

clue.text: Nigel lost in Scottish town

indicators.note: someone lost has wandered off course, so the name's letters stray from their places

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Nigel has lost his way in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgin is a town in Moray, in north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a historic cathedral town in Moray, north-east Scotland, so it fits the description of a settlement there.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts aren't nice

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the following letters go wild and are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fussy eater complaining that fruit and nuts taste bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit and nuts' reads as a snack, but nuts is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Tardy mail worried section of the MOD

indicators.note: worried in the sense of tugged and shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Late post has caused anxiety within a part of the defence ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence; the Admiralty was the department running the Royal Navy and survives as a section of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Admiralty was the naval authority, absorbed into the British defence ministry in 1964 as its navy branch.

clue.text: Old ship has permission to be on river

blocks.note: you may means you are allowed
something that flows, a crossword sense of river

explanation.surface: An old vessel is allowed to sail on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above. Reading a river as something that flows is a classic crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower was the vessel that carried the Pilgrims from England to America in 1620.

clue.text: Tracey's upset about her betrayal

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the name's letters are reshuffled
about means around, so the rearranged name surrounds the next word

blocks.note: the name rearranged, then split open
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tracey is distressed about how she was betrayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged TRACEY wraps around HER to give TREAC-HER-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is disloyalty or deception towards someone who trusted you, which is what betrayal means.

clue.text: Some thought it a nice ship

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across four words

explanation.surface: Opinions on a vessel, some people finding it pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironic understatement: the famous liner was thought unsinkable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the White Star liner that sank on its maiden voyage in 1912.

clue.text: Without sufficient warning

blocks.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-dividend, meaning without
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: Something happening with too little notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without sufficient warning' reads as one phrase, but splits into wordplay and a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone punished to deter others is made an example of, so the case serves as a caution.

clue.text: Not the first to faint and behave theatrically!

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped from the word that follows

blocks.note: a faint chance is a remote one

explanation.surface: An actor who is not the first to swoon and make a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the R from REMOTE to leave EMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to express feelings in an exaggerated, actorly way, as on a stage.

clue.text: Atrocity causes visible anger

blocks.note: out as in the stars are out, meaning able to be seen
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A terrible act provokes open fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means both the atrocity and the anger, which helps the surface read smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shockingly cruel or wicked act, the same as an atrocity.

clue.text: Mountain always initially engenders severe trepidation

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each following word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: a plain synonym, as in for ever
first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A peak that always inspires dread in climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest peak, in the Himalayas on the Nepal-Tibet border.

clue.text: Girl without single item of headgear

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the name sits around the next piece

blocks.note: a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl with no single hat to her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': TARA goes round I to give TI-A-RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, so it is a piece of headwear.

clue.text: Potassium nitrate and sodium chloride prized by soldiers

blocks.note: the chemical name for common table salt
a pet project is a prized or favourite one
the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Two chemicals valued by the army, apt since one goes into gunpowder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prized by soldiers' reads as one phrase but splits in two; the Royal Engineers are the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is the traditional name for the compound used in gunpowder, fertiliser and meat curing.

clue.text: Divided town in Croatia

blocks.note: first meaning: separated into parts
second meaning: a port city on the Dalmatian coast

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a town split by conflict; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb meaning to break apart is also the name of the Adriatic port in Croatia.

clue.text: Bars for central Europeans

blocks.note: first meaning: long rods or posts
second meaning: people from Poland

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like pubs aimed at visitors; with a capital, the word means people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Long rods are called by this word, and with a capital it names natives of Poland in central Europe.

clue.text: Nervously put in a line for marriage

indicators.note: done nervously means fidgety and unsteady, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: put, in and a taken as written, with line giving L, the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Anxiously queueing up to get married.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial is the adjective describing anything relating to a wedding, such as a nuptial mass or blessing.

clue.text: We shall finally get on benefits

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it follows, keeping just that letter

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of shall
to fare is to get on, as in how did you fare

explanation.surface: A defiant claim that we shall manage once we are living on state payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We shall' looks like it should become WE'LL, but only the last letter of shall is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is state financial support for those in need, the same thing as social security payments.

clue.text: Mild chap

blocks.note: first meaning: gentle, especially of weather
second meaning: a man's given name

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a gentle man; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is pleasant and gentle, and Clement is also a man's first name, borne by several popes.

clue.text: About half of spectators show appreciation

indicators.note: half of a word means only its first portion of letters is used

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
the first five of its ten letters

explanation.surface: Roughly half the crowd at a game applauding.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect is admiration or high regard for someone, close in sense to appreciation of their worth.
